title: Chapter 72 — Scaling the Book
intro: From a handful of accounts to a mature book of business — systemizing, delegating, and building the machine.

sections.title: The Capacity Wall
sections.content:
At some point, your trade book grows beyond what one person can manage at a high level. When you have 20+ active accounts, each needing quoting, delivery coordination, and relationship maintenance, something starts to slip. Quote turnaround slows. Follow-ups get missed. Job site visits become infrequent.

This is the capacity wall. You have two choices: cap your growth (and your income), or systematize to handle more volume without sacrificing service quality.

sections.title: Systematizing the Book
sections.content:
Template your quotes — standardized packages at pre-set tiers reduce quoting time from 30 minutes to 10. Create delivery coordination checklists that your operations team can execute without your involvement on every detail.

Tier your accounts. Tier 1 gets your personal attention on every project. Tier 2 gets your attention on kickoff and closeout, with your support team handling mid-project coordination. Tier 3 gets systematized service — standard quotes, standard delivery, standard follow-up.

This is not reducing service. It is allocating your highest-value time — relationship building and problem solving — where it produces the most return.

sections.title: Building the Machine
sections.content:
The ultimate scale move is building a trade desk team. You become the trade desk lead. You bring in a coordinator to handle quoting and logistics. You bring in a junior trade rep to manage Tier 3 accounts and develop into handling Tier 2.

Your income shifts from personal production to team production. You earn on the book's total revenue, not just your individual sales. This is how trade specialists become six-figure earners — not by selling harder, but by building a machine that sells systematically.
